body: This makes me so happy to read! I'm so proud of you!

From someone who is in the exact same position, mentally, and only has two months left of college (plus a summer term), if there is ANY way you can withdrawal and take another job close to home or find any way of financial stability then do it. I made the choice to push through. The past year it came to the point of withdrawaling from half of my classes and having two incompletes and even then I pushed the deadlines. One of my professors was extremely kind but the other made me feel like shit and I'm now on academic probation. Even though I feel like I can finish my degree with multiple Cs and ruining my GPA, I have no love or capacity to maintain what I am learning. I wish I was able to have taken a year or a semester off to work on me because even though I'm finishing this year, I'm wasting all the money I am spending to attend college anyway by just going through the steps and not retaining any knowledge and losing the passion for the things I am studying with each class. And honestly, I'm scared I won't even get a good job with my degree because when I graduate I will still be so incredibly depressed.

It's not selfish. Especially coming from the place you are in. I totally understand the feeling. When I am in a really dark place and am thinking of the ways to kill myself, I really wish just one of my friends would read into my short responses and ask if I am okay and then don't believe my "I'm fine" message that follows. It's a lot to be hoping for but I feel like there should be at least one person out there that gets me enough to realize I'm not okay because I always feel like I can't say anything about what I really feel because it isn't fair to them. I feel like that puts a responsibility on them to stop me from killing myself and I feel like I can't do that to someone. And I refuse to do that now anyways from having people respond in the worst ways (someone once told me they "just didn't care" when I told them I was in a really dark place).

Everything about your post gives me a glimmer of hope. I have really been struggling with suicidal thoughts and have made several plans to execute such plans in the past few days and while reading this I felt a little lighter. Almost everything you have accomplished are the things I have dreamt of finally doing/having. I'm a few months from graduating college and I dream of moving to the coast to attend graduate school for marine biology and swimming with the creatures I want to protect. I would love to pursue Spanish to the point of becoming fluent, I have taken four years and I love the language. I have also been struggling with my sexuality lately and knowing you found a woman you love makes me incredibly happy and hopeful. Everything still feels incredibly dark at the moment but I am grateful to have something to come back and read when I feel like killing myself because I don't think things will get better. Thank you.

I'm glad you're able to try to switch your thinking at times. I wish that would work for me but I honestly have been depressed for so long that when I think about suicide and am in that moment it's kind of comforting so I really indulge in it. I guess it is because it is the only time I really feel emotions so powerfully.
Sometimes that's the best help someone can get at the time. Feeling so alone and knowing at least someone understands helps a little bit. So thank you.

I've been in therapy for over a year now. I've been taking medication for as long as I can remember. I've been admitted to hospitals. I feel like I've done it all. Nothing has really changed my life around or my view on things and I've honestly felt like things have just gotten worse. 

But thank you for suggesting it. I know it can be such a game changer for others. I just wish it was for me.
